title: The Kitchen of Bellbird Bay
premise: Dominic Marchetti, a ghostwriter who keeps love in the past tense, is hired to anonymously pen the memoirs of Vivian Ashford — the ruthless developer evicting half of Bellbird Bay, including the bakery run by Marisol Reyes, Dominic's estranged first love. Through exchanged manuscript pages and unsigned letters, Dominic and Marisol fall for each other all over again without realizing they are already entangled: she is suing his client, and he is writing the woman destroying her livelihood. When Marisol discovers his betrayal, Dominic must choose between the contract that funds his silence about his own past and testifying to Vivian's forged lease documents. In the end he burns the memoir's final chapter, testifies outside the safety of anonymity, and wins back Marisol as the bakery's lease is saved.
about_author: Jude Villalobos is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming one of their own. They live near the coast, where every draft begins with coffee and ends with bread.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A ghostwriter who never signs his name takes a lucrative anonymous memoir contract in Bellbird Bay, hiding from a scandal in his own past. He glimpses Marisol Reyes through her bakery window and walks away. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Assignment
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Her landlord's lawyer delivers an eviction notice tied to developer Vivian Ashford's waterfront project. That same week, a literary agency pairs Marisol with an anonymous pen-pal 'for creative renewal' — a program secretly run by Dominic's editor. Emotional beat: defiance kindling under fear.

chapters.title: Letters Without Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pen pals exchange letters; each unknowingly writes to the person they can't forgive or forget. Dominic recognizes Marisol's voice by chapter three of her letters but says nothing. Emotional beat: dangerous intimacy growing inside anonymity.

chapters.title: Flour and Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts the anonymous memoirist's research assistant snooping around her bakery for 'local color' — it's Dominic, collecting material for Vivian's book. Old wounds reopen; neither admits the letter connection. Emotional beat: anger braided with longing.

chapters.title: What the Memoir Omits
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Digging through Vivian's archives, Dominic finds a forged lease signature predating the eviction — proof the whole redevelopment rests on fraud. Writing the truth would end his career; omitting it makes him complicit. Emotional beat: conscience versus survival.

chapters.title: The Midnight Batch
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. On eviction eve, Marisol bakes through the night and finds a letter slipped under her door — her pen pal confessing he's nearby, asking to meet. She almost goes, then sees Dominic leaving Vivian's offices across the street. Emotional beat: hope curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Two Truths at the Table
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Cornered by coincidence, Dominic confesses everything to Marisol: the ghostwriting, the letters, the forgery he found. She calls him a coward with good handwriting and walks out. Emotional beat: devastating honesty arriving too late.

chapters.title: Power Corrupts the Draft
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Vivian offers Marisol a generous settlement and the pen-pal letters' publication rights — if she drops the suit and hands over Dominic's drafts as leverage. Marisol realizes Vivian has known about the letters all along. Emotional beat: temptation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Chapter
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the public hearing, Dominic burns the memoir's final chapter on camera, forfeits his fee and anonymity, and testifies to the forged lease. Marisol, given the chance to bury him with his drafts, instead submits them as evidence. Emotional beat: both risking the whole heart at once.

chapters.title: Bellbird Bay Rising
chapters.summary: Resolution, alternating POV. The forgery voids the eviction; Vivian's empire cracks under investigation. Dominic signs his own name to a novel for the first time, set in a bakery. In the rebuilt kitchen, he asks Marisol for a future in present tense. Emotional beat: love finally signed, sealed, and rising like dough.
